newsitem.title: CHINA: INTERVIEW-China banker sees $10 bln trade surplus.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-China banker sees $10 bln trade surplus.

text.p: China's central bank governor said he expected the renminbi to remain stable although he saw upward pressure on the Chinese currency, partly due to an expected trade surplus of over $10 billion this year.

Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China, also said there was no fixed timetable for making the currency convertible on the capital account, adding it probably would take a fairly long time.
"I can assure you that for a considerable period of time the exchange rate of the Chinese currency will be stable," Dai told Reuters in an interview on Tuesday.
"There will be some pressure for appreciation though," he said.
The renminbi currently trades at about 8.3 to one dollar.
"Total foreign trade will climb substantially this year and frankly speaking, we could have a trade surplus of more than $10 billion," he said.
The trade surplus would be down sharply from last year's $16.7 billion surplus but would be a big improvement from forecasts made earlier this year.
